name: Music recording and production session
one_line: A bounded song or release being recorded and produced through session files, takes, edits, stems, mixes, masters, rights paperwork and delivery variants; a working session may reference audio it does not contain and mix versions multiply.

deterministic: A readable DAW session or interchange file whose tracks, clips, takes, playlists or regions reference recorded audio, instrument parts, samples or stems, with a recurring song, artist or release identifier in session metadata or labelled companion text.
A coherent packet linking a recording/session manifest or track sheet to take-numbered audio, an editable DAW session, mix notes or recalls, and named stereo, instrumental, acapella or stem exports.

A mix or master delivery record that names exact audio files, sample rate, bit depth, channel layout or platform variants and is paired with the corresponding render; `FINAL` without an artifact-bearing record is insufficient.

A rights or metadata packet that names a recording, contributors, splits, ISRC/UPC-like identifiers, territory or usage grant and is linked to the session or delivery by the same release reference. This is recognition of a music-production neighbourhood, not a licence fact written by this fieldless schema.

A project archive whose manifest contains an editable session, audio takes, edits, stems, recall notes, masters and delivery metadata, even when some referenced media or plug-ins are absent. Archive paths alone never supply a music-session conclusion.
needs_llm: deciding whether a DAW session is a song, podcast, film score, game audio, sound-design pass, rehearsal, lecture or private voice memo when the surrounding purpose is not labelled
matching take numbers, track names, stems and mix recalls when filenames use abbreviated or conflicting conventions
deciding whether a bounced WAV is a work-in-progress, review mix, approved master, live recording or an isolated reference track
distinguishing a recording-rights or royalty document from a generic contract, invoice or business record when the same artist and title occur in both
deciding whether a session archive is complete when linked audio, samples, plug-ins, licences or external drives are missing
never_alone: a `.logicx`, `.ptx`, `.als`, `.flac`, `.wav`, `.aiff`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.cue` or `.zip` extension; extensions route extraction and do not establish a music project
the words song, track, take, mix, master, stem, vocal, beat, session, bounce, release or approved alone
an artist, band, producer, engineer, label or studio name alone
`FINAL`, `MASTER`, `MIX 3`, `v2`, `R2` or `approved` in a filename; version_family is universal metadata and approval requires linked artifact evidence
a waveform, duration, BPM, key, codec, loudness value or embedded album tag alone
a folder named Audio, Sessions, Masters, Mixes, Songs or Releases, or membership in one download/export session
a screenshot of a mixer or timeline without recoverable song, session or release context
a bare date or four-digit number interpreted as recording date, release year, catalogue number or take number

grouping_reasons: one song or release across tracking sessions, take families, edits, stems, mix recalls, masters and delivery variants
one recording date or session whose takes are recoverably named by track, performer or slate
one mix-review cycle where notes name the exact bounce and a later recall or render responds to them
one delivery set whose manifest names exact masters, formats, channels, metadata and destination variants
overlapping membership of a music-production group and a universal version_family is expected; sparse audio must not receive song or stage facts copied from a nearby session

template.why: Empty by binding contract: the creative schema declares no field rows, so project, stage, artifact_type, work_type, artist and release cannot become authored folder dimensions here. The recommended lifecycle is session/tracking → takes and edits → stems → mix/recall → master → rights and metadata → delivery, but these are work-type or stage values for later schema adjudication, not paths or facts this placeholder may write. It is not time-first: recording date, session date, mix date and release date are different workflow clocks, and filesystem time cannot order them.

collides_with.signal: The same session/mix fixture can be read as generic post-production: a DAW project, stems, review notes and a master export. Music-session activation requires recording-specific evidence such as take/playlist families, track or performer roles, song/release identifiers, or music delivery variants; post-production must not infer a song merely from a mix, stem or WAV. Conversely, a song session with those recording signals must not be flattened into generic post-production and lose take and rights context. Shared fixture: North Star_S04_Stems_2026-07-18.zip and North Star_S04_Mix_Recall_03.pdf.

A sound-design session may also contain WAVs, tracks, stems, recalls and a mix. The discriminator is whether audio is being made as a song/release with takes, performers, song metadata and music delivery variants, or to sit under picture/game/installation with scene, timecode, cue, foley or effects evidence. The same Harbour Film_Sound_Mix_05.aaf must remain sound-design/post-production evidence, while North Star_S04_Mix_Recall_03.pdf must not be claimed by sound design solely because it contains mix notes.

Both domains use recording sessions, edits, mixes and delivery files. A podcast episode is activated by episode/show cadence, spoken-word edit, transcript/show notes or publish record; a music session by takes, overdubs, instrumental/acapella/stem structure and song/release metadata. A file named `Final Mix.wav` alone is ambiguous in both directions and falls through until its surrounding evidence is recoverable.

Audio/video media can carry capture metadata and can be a personal recording. A phone or field recorder file with only device metadata is not a music session; a recording session becomes music evidence only with the track/take/session structure described above. The reciprocal photos boundary is that audio capture metadata must not acquire a photo event or music project from nearby filenames.

A finished master, showreel excerpt or artist portfolio can be both a made artifact and a career presentation. The making-side evidence is session/take/revision/delivery structure; the career-side evidence is curated self-presentation, resume, reel or application purpose. A lone master such as North Star_S04_Master_24bit_44k1.wav must not be moved into a portfolio or music branch based on content alone.

Generative music repositories and software build outputs may contain audio renders, version tokens and words such as render or release. Repository markers, manifests and source code explain the code domain; DAW tracks, linked takes and mix/master records explain this row. `build-release-notes.md` remains code evidence even if it mentions audio rendering.

also_holds_with.signal: A signed split sheet, producer agreement, sample licence or artist release can be a legal instrument and a rights record attached to a music session. The legal reading must retain parties, execution and operative clauses; the music reading may group it with the named recording. Neither reading may suppress the other.

A label or studio production packet may be both a music-making record and an operational record with approvals, budgets, purchase orders or reporting. DAW/take/mix evidence supports this row; controlled headers, accounting tables or approval workflow support business_operations. Shared names and project references do not collapse the two.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone master, session file or rights sheet with durable purpose but no recoverable song/session association belongs in the residual rather than a synthetic music project.
Unattached mix notes, incomplete manifests, unsigned split sheets and ambiguous delivery messages need a future decision when the recording cannot be reconstructed.
A downloaded beat, reference track, sample or playlist item with no current recording structure is reference material, not a session.
A lone voice memo or field recording without production evidence is not music-session material merely because it is audio.
Unreleased recordings, contributor identities, private vocals and rights paperwork can remain sensitive even when the session association is unresolved.
Unreadable DAW packages, password-protected delivery archives and missing-media sessions should be represented safely rather than treated as empty or confidently filed.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased songs and mixes, raw vocals, performer identities, private communications, contractual splits and delivery metadata can expose confidential creative work or third-party personal information. Privacy handling must precede model or connector exposure; this row assigns no handling class and writes no creative fields.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: whether music should later receive `project`, `stage` and `artifact_type` through a ratified creative schema, or remain a fieldless applicability record whose session → takes → mix/master → rights/delivery lifecycle is assembled by P9/P10. A separate rights field may be useful but must not be invented here; rights instruments can also be legal records. Also unresolved: whether spoken-word music-adjacent releases should be one podcast/music boundary or a user-confirmed overlap. Recommended: retain this placeholder, use recording-specific evidence for activation, and keep sparse audio in Review Later until a session or release association is recoverable.
